subject: biology
topicDisplay: Theme D · Organisms & Ecosystems (Reproduction, Inheritance, Homeostasis, Selection, Climate)
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Sexual reproduction increases variation because it involves:
options: Meiosis and fusion of gametes from two parents
questions.explain: Meiosis and fertilisation combine alleles from two parents.

questions.q: Asexual reproduction produces offspring that are:
questions.explain: Asexual reproduction produces clones.

questions.q: Fertilisation restores the diploid number by fusing:
options: A haploid and a diploid cell
questions.explain: Two haploid gametes form a diploid zygote.

questions.q: An allele is:
questions.explain: Different alleles may give different characteristics.

questions.q: An organism with two different alleles of a gene is:
questions.explain: Homozygous means two identical alleles.

questions.q: A cross of two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt × Tt) gives a phenotype ratio of tall:short of:
questions.explain: Genotypes 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt give 3 tall : 1 short.

questions.q: Red–green colour blindness is more common in males because the allele is:
options: Recessive and carried on the X chromosome
questions.explain: Males have one X, so a single recessive allele is expressed.

questions.q: The observable characteristics of an organism are its:
questions.explain: Phenotype results from genotype and environment.

questions.q: Homeostasis is the maintenance of:
options: A stable internal environment within narrow limits
Identical gene expression in all cells
questions.explain: It keeps variables such as temperature and glucose near set points.

questions.q: Blood glucose is lowered by the hormone:
questions.explain: Insulin promotes glucose uptake and storage; glucagon raises glucose.

questions.q: When too hot, skin blood vessels:
questions.explain: Vasodilation and sweating increase heat loss.

questions.q: When blood glucose falls, glucagon causes the liver to:
options: Break down glycogen and release glucose
questions.explain: Insulin and glucagon act antagonistically by negative feedback.

questions.q: Natural selection acts on variation that is:
questions.explain: Only heritable variation changes allele frequencies over generations.

questions.q: An individual's fitness refers to its:
questions.explain: Fitness is the ability to survive and reproduce.

questions.q: The rise of dark peppered moths during industrial pollution illustrates:
options: Natural selection through a changed environment
questions.explain: Better-camouflaged moths survived and reproduced more.

questions.q: A stable ecosystem is one that:
options: Maintains structure and function despite disturbance
questions.explain: Stability includes resistance and resilience.

questions.q: Removing a keystone species usually causes:
questions.explain: Keystone species have effects out of proportion to their abundance.

questions.q: The main greenhouse gas from burning fossil fuels is:
questions.explain: Rising CO2 enhances the greenhouse effect.

questions.q: The enhanced greenhouse effect warms the planet because greenhouse gases:
questions.explain: They absorb and re-emit infrared, warming the lower atmosphere.

questions.q: Rising sea temperatures cause coral bleaching because corals:
options: Expel their symbiotic algae, losing colour and food
questions.explain: Heat stress breaks the coral–algae symbiosis and can kill coral.
